title: What is good: test discipline and oracle independence
description:
The workspace's test discipline is exemplary and worth defending against 'just test the round-trip' simplification pressure:

1. Every test module documents its independent oracle: openssl x509 -text output for serial lengths, python hashlib for SHA hashes, hand-computed DER bytes for wire-format assertions, PKITS NIST fixtures for integration coverage. No test uses the code under test as its own oracle.

2. The serde_der module's tests verify against hand-computed base64 and DER bytes, not against re-encoding. The binary-serializer test (line 424) builds a minimal Serializer impl to verify the helper takes the non-human-readable branch — this level of branch-coverage specificity catches subtle mode bugs that a JSON-only round-trip would miss.

3. CRL signer_discovery tests exercise order-independence (same result regardless of bundle ordering) and edge cases (empty bundle, unrelated bundle) with PKITS fixtures.

4. The pkix-ct verify.rs tests use hand-decoded RFC 6962 wire layouts as byte-literal expectations, and the precert TBS-reconstruction test cross-validates against a Python oracle script that independently strips the SCT extension from the cert.

5. Lint tests in pkix-lint/src/rfc5280.rs use openssl-derived oracles for fixture serial lengths and extension shapes, and the parametric lint (Rfc5280MaxSerialLengthLint) has regression tests that verify both the constructor and set_parameter reject out-of-range values.

This is the test discipline section of AGENTS.md ('no test may use the code under test as its own oracle') made real. Someone suggesting 'just encrypt-then-decrypt' style testing should be pointed here.
